rows.label: Share of the ASPCA's 2025 policy, response and engagement spending that went on farm animals

source.title: ASPCA consolidated financial statements 2025 (audited), note 2, program services
source.quote: the National Field Response team, which conducts animal field investigations and response efforts nationwide; Farm Animal Welfare; and grant-making efforts

rows.explainer: Our judgment, read by both of charityevals' ASPCA models so the split is one number: the farm-animal model's cost is this share of the $67.5m policy, response and engagement line, the companion-animal model's the rest. The accounts don't split the line by department. Anchor: Farm Animal Welfare is one of about a dozen departments in the line (field and disaster response, government relations, legal advocacy and cruelty response, humane law enforcement, forensics, behaviour rehabilitation, two recovery centres, policy operations and grants, Form 990 Schedule O); its grants are small (about $0.3m in 2025: the Fund to End Factory Farming's $160,305, Food Animal Concerns Trust $72,000, the Veterinary Association for Farm Animal Welfare $48,660), so its cost is mostly a policy and corporate team of perhaps 20 to 40 staff at about $150,000 each with overheads in the line, $3m to $8m: 8%, 4% to 14%.

rows.label: Share of the ASPCA's 2025 public education and communications spending on farm animals

source.title: ASPCA Form 990 for 2025, Schedule O, Part III line 4b
source.quote: PUBLIC EDUCATION & COMMUNICATIONS SUPPORTED THE ASPCA'S MISSION BY EDUCATING THE PUBLIC, ENGAGING SUPPORTERS, STRENGTHENING AWARENESS OF ANIMAL WELFARE ISSUES

rows.explainer: Our judgment, read by both ASPCA models: the share of the $90.0m public education line (mostly mail, television and digital about dogs, cats and horses) given to farm animals, such as the Shop With Your Heart consumer guide and factory-farming messaging. Its 2025 report on public education names only companion-animal campaigns: 3%, 1% to 6%.
